module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 965

For every 2-coloring of ℝ, is there an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that
all sums $a + b$ for $a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b$ have the same colour?

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/965](https://www.erdosproblems.com/965)
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Journées Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.
- [HLS17] Hindman, Neil and Leader, Imre and Strauss, Dona, Pairwise sums in colourings of the reals. Abh. Math. Semin. Univ. Hambg. (2017), 275--287.
- [Ko16] Komjáth, Péter, A certain 2-coloring of the reals. Real Anal. Exchange (2016), 227--231.
- [SWCol] Sokoup Dániel and Weiss, William, Sums and Anti-Ramsey Colourings of ℝ. https://danieltsoukup.github.io/academic/finset_colouring.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos965

/--
Erdős asks in [Er75b] if for every 2-coloring of ℝ, there is an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that
all sums $a + b$ for $a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b$ have the same colour.

In [Ko16] Péter Komjáth constructed a counterexample.
The same result was proven independently in [SWCol] by Sokoup and Weiss.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos965.lean#L42"]
theorem erdos_965 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ f : ℝ → Fin 2, ∃ A : Set ℝ, ¬ A.Countable ∧
      ∀ᵉ (a ∈ A) (b ∈ A) (c ∈ A) (d ∈ A), a ≠ b → c ≠ d → f (a + b) = f (c + d) := by
  sorry

/--
For every 2-coloring of ℝ, is there some $k ≥ 2$ and an uncountable set $A ⊆ ℝ$ such that all
sums $a_1 + \cdots + a_k$ of $k$ distinct elements of $A$ have the same colour?

In fact, in both [Ko16] and [SWCol] a single 2-coloring of ℝ is constructed such that for every
$k ≥ 2$ and every uncountable $A ⊆ ℝ$ the sums of $k$ distinct elements of $A$ are not
monochromatic.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 5]
theorem erdos_965.variants.generalization : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ f : ℝ → Fin 2, ∃ k ≥ 2, ∃ A : Set ℝ, ¬ A.Countable ∧ ∀ s t : Finset ℝ,
      ↑s ⊆ A → ↑t ⊆ A → s.card = k → t.card = k → f (s.sum id) = f (t.sum id) := by
  sorry

end Erdos965

findings.description: A co-author's surname is misspelled in two places. The [SWCol] entry in the module docstring (line 31) reads "Sokoup Dániel and Weiss, William", and the `erdos_965` docstring (line 43) says "proven independently in [SWCol] by Sokoup and Weiss". The name is Soukup (Dániel T. Soukup). This is a reference slip only; the mathematics is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The title block of the cited PDF (https://danieltsoukup.github.io/academic/finset_colouring.pdf) reads "DÁNIEL T. SOUKUP, WILLIAM WEISS". erdosproblems.com/965 also writes "Soukup and Weiss".
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "Sokoup Dániel" with "Soukup, Dániel T." in the reference list, and "Sokoup and Weiss" with "Soukup and Weiss" in the `erdos_965` docstring.

reformulations.difference: erdosproblems.com asks for a set A ⊆ ℝ "of cardinality ℵ₁". The Lean asks for an uncountable A (`¬ A.Countable`). The Lean also quantifies over every map `f : ℝ → Fin 2`, including non-surjective ones, where "2-colouring" might be read as using both colours.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The property "all sums a+b with a ≠ b in A have one colour" passes to subsets. Every uncountable subset of ℝ contains a subset of cardinality exactly ℵ₁ (`countable_iff_lt_aleph_one` with `le_mk_iff_exists_subset`), and a set of cardinality ℵ₁ is uncountable. So the two existence statements are equivalent for every f. A non-surjective f : ℝ → Fin 2 is constant, and then A = ℝ works, so restricting to surjective colourings changes nothing. Proved in Lean (sorry-free): `rhs_iff_aleph1` shows the ¬Countable form of the right-hand side is equivalent to the #A = ℵ₁ form, and `rhs_iff_surj` handles surjectivity. The answer polarity is right: `answer(False)` elaborates to `False`, and the source records the problem as disproved.

reformulations.difference: The variant is phrased as a question with a fixed negative answer: `False ↔ ∀ f, ∃ k ≥ 2, ∃ uncountable A` whose k-element-subset sums (Finsets of card k) are monochromatic. The literature states the positive existence of a colouring: Komjáth's corollary and Soukup–Weiss Cor. 3.2 give ∃ F : ℝ → 2 with F''{ΣE : E ∈ [X]^N} = 2 for all uncountable X and N ≥ 2. The erdosproblems remark gives HLS's result the weaker order "for any k ≥ 1 there is a colouring"; the "k ≥ 1" there is a website slip for k ≥ 2.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `False ↔ P` is `¬P`. Pushing the negation through gives ∃ f, ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ uncountable A, two k-subsets s, t of A with f(Σs) ≠ f(Σt). With two colours, that means both colours occur on FS_k(A). This is literally Soukup–Weiss Cor. 3.2, and also Komjáth's corollary: "there is a function f: ℝ→{0,1} such that if A ⊆ ℝ is uncountable, 2 ≤ k < ω, then both 0 and 1 occur as the value of f at the sum of k distinct elements of A". Proved in Lean (sorry-free) as `variant_iff_SW`. I also proved that the k = 2 instance of the Finset condition is exactly the main problem's condition (`fs2_iff`), and that the main right-hand side implies the variant's (`main_imp_variant`). So the variant's negative answer strengthens the main one. The file correctly uses k ≥ 2: with k ≥ 1 the right-hand side would be trivially true (take k = 1 and A an uncountable colour class).

review.notes:
Both statements are faithful, and both fixed answers (False) match the literature.

1. `formal_proof` link (plby/lean-proofs @ dfe2d78, line 42 = `theorem not_erdos_965`). The linked statement is `¬ RHS` of the repository theorem. I copied the full dependency chain (10 files, no `sorry`/`axiom`) and compiled it against this checkout's Mathlib (v4.33.1; the proof targets v4.33.0). It builds without errors. `#print axioms Erdos965.not_erdos_965` gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. In a scratch file importing both the FC module and the plby modules, I proved `type_of% Erdos965.erdos_965` (i.e. `False ↔ …`) from `exists_bad_real_coloring_of_finset_pair_antiramsey supportColor_finset_pair_antiramsey`, with the same three axioms. So the record is valid.

2. Status. The file says `research solved` with `answer(False)` for both theorems. erdosproblems.com says DISPROVED, and the teorth database says "disproved (Lean)". The variant rests on Komjáth (Real Anal. Exchange 41 (2016)) and Soukup–Weiss Cor. 3.2, both ZFC. There is no status issue.

3. The variant docstring says both [Ko16] and [SWCol] give a single colouring that works for all k ≥ 2. Both sources confirm this: the Komjáth abstract (via OpenAlex) and Soukup–Weiss Cor. 3.2. HLS17 proves the same uniform-in-k statement under CH, for |X| = 𝔠. erdosproblems.com's paraphrase ("for any k≥1 there is a 2-colouring") is looser than the actual results and has a k≥1 slip. The file is not affected.

4. [Er75b] is available only as a scanned PDF with no text layer (Rényi archive 1975-30.pdf), so I relied on erdosproblems.com's transcription of the question. This does not leave any declaration unsettled.

5. The only finding is the minor misspelling "Sokoup" (should be Soukup).
